svg.text: E Sub-mechanisms (3) — moving food cleanly, and proving it is clean
Each panel loops on its own. The last panel shows the shape rule that all cleaning-first mechanisms obey.
source: E-cleaning-first.md sections 0 and 6
S4 · S10 · S12 · S13 · S19 · rule C2
S4 Hourglass transfer and flip lid

g.text: preheated flip lid set on the 28 cm pan
pan + lid inverted together by the wrist
pan lifted; browned side up, slid back

svg.text: Equal rims clamped mouth to mouth and inverted: no pouring arc,
no spill, no spatula under a fragile item; also unmoulds cakes.
Feasibility H transfer, M–H flip (2.5–4 kg on the wrist)
S10 Piston box (Schubboden-Box)
Mince, quark, butter, tomato paste leave as a strand, cut by a wire,
dosed by stroke, checked by weight. The box is scraped empty
by its own floor. Feasibility M–H
S12 Witness coupon

g.text: dipped into the worst soil, dried longest
rides through the wash with the ware
coupon clean → every item is clean

svg.text: A small steel coupon soiled at the start of the meal gives a
per-cycle worst-case proof instead of process data only.
Feasibility H
S13 Vitamin-B2 self-test

g.text: mist riboflavin (vitamin B2) over clean ware
UV-A: glow left = spray shadow / blocked nozzle

svg.text: The standard spray-coverage tracer is a food vitamin: the
one-time validation becomes a weekly automatic test.
Feasibility H; 50 mL of solution a month
S19 Mirror ware and stripe inspection

g.text: electropolished tray reflects a stripe pattern
a film dulls / bends the stripes: found

svg.text: Far more sensitive than looking for colour; a plain camera.
Chooses the ware finish for inspectability (rule C11).
Feasibility M–H
Rule C2 Shapes a spray can reach

g.text: allowed (one piece or welded, radii ≥ 6 mm):
forbidden — this is where dirt hides:

svg.text: If a part is "a lathe part, a bent sheet or a laser-cut plate",
a spray or a pipe flow reaches all of it.
